name: figma-centred-title-card
exporter: Figma - Export > SVG, Include "id" attribute ON, Outline text OFF
story: The opening title card of a student documentary, every line centre-aligned on the frame's midline the way a title card always is.
idioms: text-anchor="middle" on every <text>, with the tspan's x at the CENTRE of the line (x="960" on all four) rather than at its left edge
a centred rule drawn as a <rect> whose x/width straddle the same midline
letter-spacing in em, including a NEGATIVE one on the display line (-0.01em) - Figma's optical tracking for large type
the frame contents inside <g clip-path="url(#clip0_77_310)"> with the matching <defs><clipPath><rect width height fill="white"/>, x/y omitted because it sits at the origin
no XML declaration, zero indentation, fill="none" on the root, uppercase hex, fill="white" as a keyword
xml:space="preserve" plus style="white-space: pre" on every text, fractional baselines (y="570.818")
family names without a face suffix (font-family="Archivo" + font-weight="bold"), the opposite of Illustrator
whyThisMatters: Every text-bearing file in the corpus is start-anchored except two, and in both of those the centred or end-anchored line is a detail rather than the composition. Here the anchor IS the design: four lines, all centred on one axis, and every x in the file is the middle of a line rather than its left edge. That is the coordinate a field's box, its highlight, its measured width and its too-long answer are all derived from, and reading a centred line's x as a left edge puts the box half a line to the right of the words - visible only once someone types. A title card is also the single most common thing a student makes after a lower third, so this is a shape the road meets early.
